newsitem.title: USA: CME traders call USDA data neutral for CME cattle.
newsitem.headline: CME traders call USDA data neutral for CME cattle.

text.p: CME livestock traders called the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report neutral to slightly bullish for CME live cattle because the April marketing figure of 102 percent of a year ago indicated feedlots remained current.
Traders expect CME live cattle futures to trade steady to 0.20 cent per lb higher at Monday's opening in reaction to the data.
USDA's April marketing figure was slightly greater than the 101 percent average of analysts' estimates.
The report had May 1 cattle on feed supplies at 109 percent of a year ago and April placements at 112 percent, both near the mid-range of analysts estimates.
Dale Benson, analyst with Dean Witter, called the report neutral for June cattle futures and said next week's cash cattle markets will have a greater influence on June futures than the report.
"The cash will set the tone next week and I don't expect much improvement in cash," he said, with meat packers likely to start the week bidding $66.00 per cwt, down from $67.00 trades this week.
Benson said CME August live cattle could come under pressure because feedlots increased placements of 800-lb cattle in April. These cattle should reach market-weight in August.
USDA reported 394,000 cattle weighing 800 lbs or more were placed in feedlots in April versus 386,000 in March and 296,000 a year ago.
